stem:
Lata places samples on a hard surface and hammers each one. A copper strip flattens into a thinner sheet. A lump of sulfur breaks into pieces.

Which claim about these samples is correct?

options.text: Copper is malleable because it flattens; sulfur is brittle because it breaks.
Copper is malleable; the fact that sulfur breaks can be ignored when judging sulfur.
Both samples are malleable because both changed under the hammer.
Both samples are brittle because a hammer was used on each.

teacher.key_rationale: A sample that flattens under a hammer is malleable. A sample that breaks is brittle. Flattening and breaking must both be read.
